themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked 86% last week to 13 complaints versus a 7.0-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a potential widespread ventilation, mold, or indoor pollution incident affecting multiple households across East Flatbush.
evidence: 13 complaints filed last week vs. 7.0-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 4.54)
86% spike represents statistically significant deviation from 8-week pattern
Timing coincides with seasonal weather transition or possible HVAC system failures across buildings
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents about symptoms and building conditions; check if complaints cluster geographically or by building type
Report from NYC Department of Health on whether indoor air quality complaints are being investigated; examine whether buildings are meeting ventilation codes post-COVID

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped 500% last week to 3 complaints versus a 0.5-complaint weekly average, indicating possible organized or rapid-onset destruction of street trees or private vegetation in the district.
evidence: 3 complaints filed last week vs. 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 5.0)
500% spike is among highest statistical anomalies in district this month
Pattern suggests either contractor activity, storm damage, or deliberate vandalism
reporting_angles: Canvas neighborhoods to identify which streets are affected; photograph damaged trees and identify owner (private vs. Parks Department)
Contact NYC Parks Department to determine if any tree removal or maintenance is underway; check for unpermitted contractor activity

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints skyrocketed 2300% three weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline), representing the single largest statistical spike in the 311 dataset and suggesting potential contamination, discoloration, or taste/odor issues affecting tap water.
evidence: 3 complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest severity rating)
2300% spike is the most extreme anomaly in East Flatbush 311 data
No follow-up reporting yet; timing suggests possible water main incident, lead release, or distribution contamination
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if water main breaks, flushing, or treatment changes occurred 3 weeks ago; request water quality test results
Follow up with residents who filed complaints to learn symptoms (discoloration, odor, taste) and geographic extent; check if issue has resolved or persists

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints surged 122% two weeks ago to 23 complaints versus a 10.4-complaint weekly average, indicating a significant uptick in unauthorized waste disposal across the district.
evidence: 23 complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 10.4-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 3.18)
122% increase sustained across multiple complaint categories (dumpster complaints also up 540%)
Convergence with dumpster and obstruction spikes suggests sanitation system strain
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify hotspots; visit sites to document type and scale of dumping; interview nearby residents
Contact NYC Sanitation Department to ask about enforcement actions, collection delays, or facility capacity issues; investigate whether construction or demolition activity is generating waste

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 204% two weeks ago to 65 complaints versus a 21.4-complaint weekly average, suggesting temporary but intense noise-generating activity or construction across the district.
evidence: 65 complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 21.4-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 3.52)
204% spike is third-largest anomaly by percentage in dataset
Likely tied to construction, street repair, or temporary event; pattern suggests incident is acute rather than chronic
reporting_angles: Review NYC Department of Transportation permits for road work, street flushing, or utility work 2 weeks ago
Check if complaints have subsided since spike; if ongoing, identify persistent noise sources (construction sites, transit hubs)

land_use.name: Constellation CB 17
land_use.brief: A UDAAP and disposition to facilitate a new four-story building, containing 12 residential units is being sought by HPD at 395 East 94th Street in the East Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, Community
land_use.applicant: HPD - NYC Dept of Housing Preservation & Development
